subject: Business Models
title: The Four-Day Work Week
description: A quick, practical guide to The Four-Day Work Week.

hook.text: Iceland tested a four-day work week with 2,500 workers. Productivity stayed the same or improved.

buildup.text: Companies in the UK, Japan, and New Zealand have trialed shorter weeks. Most report equal output in less time.

discovery.text: Fewer hours force efficiency. Meetings shrink, distractions decrease, and focused work increases.

twist.text: Not all industries can adopt it. Healthcare, manufacturing, and retail need coverage that four days can't provide.

climax.text: The four-day week is a business model innovation for talent: attract better people by offering better lives.

punchline.text: Same output, one less day. The four-day week is a talent acquisition strategy.

quiz.question: What did Iceland's four-day work week trial find?
options: Productivity stayed the same or improved

details.summary: The four-day work week compresses or reduces working time to four days while maintaining full salaries. Trials in the UK, Iceland, and Japan showed maintained or improved productivity with significant gains in employee well-being, reduced burnout, and lower turnover rates.
details.whyItMatters: Large-scale trials are producing compelling evidence that five-day work weeks are not optimal. Companies adopting four-day weeks report equal output with happier employees..
takeaways: Trials show maintained productivity with improved employee well-being
Revenue remained stable or increased during most four-day week pilots
Reduced burnout and turnover save companies significant replacement costs

faq.question: What did the largest four-day work week trials reveal?
faq.answer: The UK trial involving 61 companies found that 92% continued the policy after the trial. Revenue stayed stable or increased. Sick days dropped 65%. Employee well-being improved significantly. Iceland's trials covering 1% of the working population were deemed an overwhelming success.

faq.question: Why can companies maintain productivity in four days?
faq.answer: Shorter weeks force elimination of unproductive meetings and distractions. Employees are more focused and energized. Reduced burnout improves quality of work output. Companies restructure workflows to prioritize high-value tasks. The constraint of less time creates productive efficiency pressure.
